agree.reason: The letter is calm and its asks are specific and doable, and the 74-of-112 figure undercuts her view that this is a few loud people, so she will likely feel she has to answer in writing, though she may still give the second-elevator request little weight.

honest.reason: Every number comes from the brief, and the conversions hold up (one day in eight so far this year, two in three households, five months since June); the only additions are mild inferences such as 'safe when it runs' and the hypothetical upper-floor resident with a walker.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the raw figures into stronger true forms (one day in eight, two in every three households) and places the two identical six-to-eight-week promises side by side, though it doesn't spell out what another outage like August's would mean for the 29 vulnerable residents.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative to acting is shown as the facts show it: frequent outages and a part that has been 'six to eight weeks away' since June, with the passing certificate acknowledged rather than hidden, though there is no trend data to draw on.

qualification.reason: The demands carry a checkable date (December 1) and ask management to say what it will do if the part's delivery date is missed, but the letter never says what the association will do if the December 1 deadline itself passes without a reply.

objections.reason: It meets her likely objections: the inspection ('it passed'), the cost and feasibility of a second elevator (it asks for the reasoning, not a reversal) and 'a few loud people' (two-thirds of households signed), and it raises nothing the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It is an open letter of about 430 words, close to the 400 asked for, signed by the secretary and written to be posted in the lobby, though it doesn't account for the plan to send it to the TV station.
